page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. Additionally, it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating with dedicated CPU allocation, the c4d-standard-4 ensures consistent compute performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants. The lack of local NVMe storage represents an architectural tradeoff, requiring users to rely on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency depending on the selected storage tier. The absence of GPU acceleration limits its utility for hardware-accelerated workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-4 offers a balanced entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk performance. It is suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, microservices, lightweight container orchestration, and basic CI/CD pipelines where dedicated CPU execution is preferred over shared-core alternatives.
